en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Second Training Rule on Uplifting (Ukkhittakasikkhāpada).
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks sat with their robes tucked up inside a house...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I will not sit with my robe tucked up inside a house.
One must not sit with one's robe tucked up inside a house."
If one, out of disrespect, sits down inside a house after having lifted up either one side or both sides [of the robe], it is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is forgetful, one who is unaware,
For one who has entered upon the rains retreat,
for one in times of distress, and for one who is insane.
the tenth training rule is finished.
The first chapter, on "all around," is concluded.
